assessment.decisionReason: Release assurance exists, but production hardening, independent assurance, live recovery, efficacy, and operating-model gates remain open.

frameworks.name: NIST SP 800-218 Secure Software Development Framework
CSA Cloud Controls Matrix and CAIQ
NIST Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
CSA AI Consensus Assessments Initiative Questionnaire

controls.title: Technical security verification
gaps: No commissioned independent penetration test exists.
The backend suite measures 75.29 percent coverage and retains a 70 percent ratchet, below the 80 percent target; the security audit checklist is not externally attested.
The repository-wide Ruff baseline is not clean or enforced; high-severity Bandit SAST is the current blocking Python static-analysis gate.

controls.title: Release integrity, SBOM, signing, and provenance
Identity, authorization, and tenant isolation
gaps: Independent cross-tenant authorization testing remains open.

controls.title: Transport, storage encryption, and key management
gaps: Production KMS or HSM custody, rotation evidence, and deployment-specific at-rest encryption validation are organizational gates.

controls.title: Data protection, privacy, retention, and deletion
gaps: Tenant-to-region pinning and regional-cell fail-closed routing are implemented; a production-topology residency and controlled region-migration exercise remains open.
Production retention, deletion, legal-basis, and data-processing evidence require deployment and organizational controls.

controls.title: Backup, recovery, failover, and resilience
gaps: The production HA topology is not configured and backup, restore, failover, RPO, and RTO have not been exercised in a game-day.

controls.title: Operational observability and SLO evidence
gaps: Approved production SLOs, alert validation, and sustained customer-topology evidence remain open.

controls.title: Incident and vulnerability response
gaps: Named 24x7 responders, customer notification, and an exercised production incident drill are organizational gates.

controls.title: Detection efficacy, model integrity, and AI governance
gaps: The single-source prompt-injection benchmark does not establish production efficacy across multilingual, multi-turn, indirect-injection, tool-call, or customer distribution shift.
Attack-graph and anomaly detection still lack independent efficacy evidence.

externalGates.title: Independent penetration test
externalGates.acceptanceCriteria: Signed final report covers the control plane, runtime agent, SDK trust boundary, tenant isolation, model endpoints, and production deployment; critical and high findings are closed or CISO-accepted.

externalGates.title: Production-topology recovery and failover exercise
externalGates.acceptanceCriteria: Signed game-day evidence proves approved RPO and RTO, restore integrity, audit-chain continuity, service failover, and detection continuity.

externalGates.title: Production-representative independent efficacy evaluation
externalGates.acceptanceCriteria: Approved multi-corpus and design-partner evaluation reports precision, recall, false-positive rate, detection latency, confidence intervals, and known limits for every promoted detection surface.

externalGates.title: Support, incident, SLO, and escalation readiness
externalGates.acceptanceCriteria: Named support and security rotations, tested escalation and notification procedures, approved SLOs, alert catalog, status communications, and exercised incident evidence are retained.

externalGates.title: Organizational, privacy, and legal assurance
externalGates.acceptanceCriteria: Approved customer evidence package includes applicable SOC 2 or ISO evidence, SIG or CAIQ responses, DPA, privacy and residency terms, subprocessors, insurance, accessibility, and license terms.

externalGates.title: Production hardening and enterprise identity promotion
externalGates.acceptanceCriteria: The 80 percent coverage goal passes, data residency and fairness controls are implemented, and release-candidate deployment evidence is retained.
